title: Bump-and-hole engineering of human polypeptide N-acetylgalactosamine transferases to dissect their protein substrates and glycosylation sites in cells
protocol: Pick a single colony from the transformed bacteria and inoculate a 3 mL culture of LB medium containing the appropriate selection antibiotic.
Incubate the culture at 37°C for at least 6 hours in a shaking incubator at >200 rpm.
Transfer 2 mL of the culture into a 15 mL centrifuge tube and centrifuge at >10,000 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Use the QIAprep Spin Miniprep Kit and a microcentrifuge to purify plasmid DNA according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Confirm the presence of the point mutation and the absence of any undesired mutations by Sanger Sequencing.
Repeat steps 1–3 to introduce the second point mutation.
Inoculate a positive colony into a 100 mL culture of LB medium containing the appropriate selection antibiotic.
Incubate at 37°C for at least 6 h in a shaking incubator at >200 rpm.
Purify plasmid DNA by Maxiprep using the ZymoPURE™ II Plasmid Maxiprep Kit and a vacuum manifold according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Express His-tagged truncated WT and BH GalNAc-T in Expi293F™ cells.
Transfect the cells with expression plasmids coding His-tagged truncated WT and BH GalNAc-T using the ExpiFectamine™ 293 Transfection Kit according to manufacturer’s instructions.
After four days, centrifuge the cells at 200 × g for 5 min.
Collect and filter the supernatant.
Add 1 mM NiSO4 to the collected supernatant.
Purify His-tagged truncated WT and BH GalNAc-T by Ni-NTA purification.
Incubate for 15 minutes at 4°C on a tube roller shaker.
Condition Ni-NTA® Agarose beads three times with 5 column volumes of water.
Condition Ni-NTA® Agarose beads twice with 5 column volumes of Wash buffer.
Add the supernatant to the beads.
Incubate the samples for 16–20 hours at 4°C on a tube roller shaker.
Wash the beads three times with 10 column volumes of Wash Buffer.
Elute the protein by adding 2 column volumes of 20% Elution Buffer (100 mM imidazole).
Elute the protein by adding 2 column volumes of 40% Elution Buffer (200 mM imidazole).
Elute the protein by adding another 2 column volumes of 40% Elution Buffer (200 mM imidazole).
Elute the protein by adding 2 column volumes of 60% Elution Buffer (300 mM imidazole).
Dialyze the eluted protein for 16–20 hours using SnakeSkin™ Dialysis Tubing against Freezing Buffer.
Determine the protein concentration.
Aliquot, flash-freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C.
Mix reagents in PCR tubes as specified.
Incubate at 37°C for 16–20 hours.
Quench by heating at 95°C for 10 seconds before placing on ice.
Determine glycopeptide formation by HPLC-MS and MS+ peak integration.
Calculate the conversion using signal integration.
Handle the enzyme on ice.
Add the enzyme to the reaction mixture last.
Determine the enzyme concentration at which ∼10%–20% glycopeptide formation is achieved.
Set up in vitro glycosylation reactions using different WT and BH GalNAc-T concentrations: 2 nM, 4 nM, 8 nM, 16 nM, 32 nM, 64 nM.
Incubate at 37°C for 1.5 hours.
Quench the reaction by heating at 95°C for 10 seconds before placing on ice.
Determine glycopeptide formation by HPLC-MS and MS+ peak integration using Equation 1.
Set up in vitro glycosylation reactions using the determined enzyme concentration and different UDP-sugar concentrations: 15.6 μM, 32.2 μM, 62.5 μM, 125 μM, 250 μM, 500 μM.
Increase the peptide concentration to at least twice the Km to ensure it is present in excess.
Incubate at 37°C for 1.5 hours.
Quench the reaction by heating at 95°C for 10 seconds before placing on ice.
Determine glycopeptide formation by HPLC-MS and MS+ peak integration using Equation 1.
Divide the measured glycopeptide formation over the duration of the reaction (5400 s) to calculate the initial rate of reaction at each substrate concentration.
Determine the kinetic parameters for the BH GalNAc-T/compound 1 and WT GalNAc-T/UDP-GalNAc pairs.
Use non-linear Michaelis-Menten and kcat fitting programs found in GraphPad Prism.
Handle the enzyme on ice.
Add the enzyme to the reaction mixture last.
Prepare a linearized vector by restriction digestion using SfiI according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Amplify the target fragment (i.e., WT/BH GalNAc-T) by PCR.
Use CloneAmp HiFi PCR Premix according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Analyze linearized vector and PCR product by agarose gel electrophoresis.
Confirm presence of a single band at expected molecular weight.
Purify linearized vector using NucleoSpin® Gel and PCR Clean-up Kit.
Follow manufacturer’s instructions for purification kit.
Purify PCR products using NucleoSpin® Gel and PCR Clean-up Kit.
Follow manufacturer’s instructions for purification kit.
Set up In-Fusion cloning reaction.
Use In-Fusion® HD Cloning kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Transform the cloning reaction products using Stellar™ Competent Cells according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Pick a single colony from the transformed bacteria and inoculate a 3 mL culture of LB medium containing the appropriate selection antibiotic.
Streak an appropriate selection agar plate before placing the tip into the LB culture as a backup.
Incubate at 37°C for at least 6 h (preferably 16–20 h) in a shaking incubator at >200 rpm.
Transfer 2 mL of the culture into a 15 mL centrifuge tube and centrifuge at >10000 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Use the QIAprep Spin Miniprep Kit and a microcentrifuge to purify plasmid DNA according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Confirm the success of the In-Fusion Cloning reaction by Sanger Sequencing.
Inoculate a 100 mL culture of LB medium containing the appropriate selection antibiotic with a positive colony.
Incubate at 37°C for at least 6 h in a shaking incubator at >200 rpm.
Purify plasmid DNA by Maxiprep using the ZymoPURE™ II Plasmid Maxiprep Kit and a vacuum manifold according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Plate K-562 cells at 70%–90% confluency in 1.5 mL of growth medium in a 6-well plate.
Transfect the cells with Lipofectamine LTX according to the manufacturer’s instructions using 2.4 μg pSBbi plasmid and 125 ng pCMV(CAT)T7-SB100 plasmid DNA per well.
Include control of transient vs stable expression using 2.4 μg pSBbi plasmid but no pCMV(CAT)T7-SB100 plasmid DNA.
Incubate cells at 37°C for 16–20 h.
Harvest the cells and resuspend in 2 mL of growth medium containing 150 μg/mL hygromycin B.
Maintain selection for 7–10 days to establish stable colonies.
Change to fresh media containing 150 μg/mL hygromycin B every two days.
Reduce the hygromycin B concentration in the growth medium to 100 μg/mL once controls have died.
Prepare a diluted Lipofectamine LTX solution using 15 μL of Lipofectamine LTX Reagent and 150 μL of Opti-MEM Medium.
Dilute plasmid DNA in 150 μL of Opti-MEM Medium.
Add 14 μL of PLUS™ Reagent to the diluted DNA solution.
Optional: Filter the diluted DNA solution using a 0.2 μM PES syringe filter before adding PLUS™ Reagent.
Plate stably transfected K-562 cells at a density of 4 × 10^5 cells/mL in 1.6 mL of growth medium without hygromycin B into a 6-well plate.
Feed cells with 50 μM compound 2, 50 μM Ac4ManNAl as a positive control, and DMSO vehicle as a negative control.
Incubate cells at 37°C for another 20 hours.
Centrifuge cells for 5 minutes at 500 × g and 4°C.
Resuspend cells in 200 μL of ice-cold 2% FBS in 1× PBS.
Transfer the suspension to a V-shaped 96-well plate.
Centrifuge for 3 min at 500 × g and 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash cells twice with 200 μL of ice-cold 2% FBS in 1× PBS.
Resuspend cells in 35 μL of 2% FBS in 1× PBS.
Treat cells with 35 μL of 2× CuAAC solution I.
Incubate the mixture for 7 min at 20°C–25°C on an orbital shaker.
Quench the CuAAC reaction with 35 μL of quenching solution.
Centrifuge for 3 min at 500 × g and 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash cells twice with 200 μL of PBS.
Resuspend cells in 100 μL of ice-cold lysis buffer I.
Lyse cells for 20 min at 4°C on an orbital shaker.
Centrifuge for 20 min at 1500 × g and 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new plate.
Measure protein concentration by BCA.
Treat equal amounts of protein (typically 15 μg) with PNGase F (4 μL of diluted PNGase F solution).
Make up the treated samples to 40 μL with lysis buffer I.
Incubate samples for 16–20 h at 37°C.
Quench by heating at 95°C for 10 s before placing on ice.
Add 4× loading buffer to each sample.
Dilute 3 parts of sample with 1 part of 4× loading buffer so that the final concentration of loading buffer in the mixture is 1×.
Run the samples on a 4%–20% gel for SDS-PAGE.
Incubate the gel in fixing solution for 10 min at 20°C–25°C on an orbital shaker.
Wash the gel once with deionized water.
Image the gel on a fluorescence gel imager.
Incubate the gel in SafeBlue Protein Stain for 30 min to assess total protein content.
Discard SafeBlue Protein Stain.
Wash the gel twice with deionized water.
Image the gel on a fluorescence gel imager.
Add 4× loading buffer to each sample.
Boil samples at 95°C for 5 min.
Run the samples on a 4%–20% gel for SDS-PAGE.
Transfer the gel to a nitrocellulose membrane.
Use the Trans-Blot Turbo Transfer System according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Select the MIXED MW protocol (5–150 kDa, 7 min, 2.5 A constant up to 25 V for 2 Mini Gels or 1 Midi Gel / 2.5 A constant up to 25 V for 1 Mini Gel).
Leave the membrane to dry to maximize protein retention.
Wet the membrane with deionized water until fully hydrated.
Incubate the membrane in 5 mL of Revert™ 700 Total Protein Stain for 5 min.
Rinse the membrane twice with 5 mL of Revert™ 700 Wash Solution.
Wash the membrane with deionized water.
Image the membrane on a fluorescence gel imager.
Incubate the membrane in 5 mL of Revert™ Destaining Solution for 5 min.
Wash the membrane with deionized water.
Incubate the membrane in blocking buffer for 1 h at 20°C–25°C.
Perform antibody staining.
Image the membrane on a fluorescence gel imager.
Cover samples with aluminum foil once CuAAC solution is added due to light sensitivity of CF680 picolyl azide.
Do not leave Revert™ Destaining Solution for longer than 10 minutes.
Treat cell lysates with PNGase F prior to analysis to remove N-glycans.
Plate stably transfected cells at a density of 2.4 × 10^5 cells/mL in 25 mL of growth medium without hygromycin B into a 15 cm dish.
Incubate cells for 16–20 h at 37°C to allow the cells to adhere to the plate.
Feed cells with 10 μM compound 3 or DMSO.
Incubate cells at 37°C for another 20 h.
Discard media.
Wash cells with 5 mL of PBS.
Incubate cells for 10 min with 8 mM EDTA in 1× PBS.
Detach cells by pipetting using a 1 mL pipette and transfer to a centrifuge tube on ice.
Centrifuge cells for 5 min at 500 × g and 4°C.
Wash cells with 200 μL of PBS.
Centrifuge for 3 min at 500 × g and 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat wash with PBS.
Resuspend cells in 200 μL of ice-cold lysis buffer II.
Lyse the cells for 20 min at 4°C on an orbital shaker.
Centrifuge for 20 min at 1500 × g and 4°C.
Transfer supernatant to low-bind tubes.
Measure protein concentration by BCA.
Dilute equal amounts of protein to 250 μL with PBS.
Transfer 300 μL of Sera-Mag SpeedBeads Neutravidin-Coated Magnetic Beads slurry to low-bind tubes.
Place the tubes on a magnetic rack and wait until beads migrate to tube wall.
Discard supernatant.
Add 200 μL of PBS.
Vortex briefly to resuspend beads.
Spin down to ensure all solution is at bottom of tube.
Place the tubes on a magnetic rack and discard the supernatant.
Repeat wash with 200 μL of PBS.
Add samples to the beads.
Vortex briefly to ensure beads are in solution.
Incubate for 2 h at 20°C–25°C under rotation.
Spin down to ensure all solution is at bottom of tube.
Place the tubes on a magnetic rack.
Collect supernatant.
Dilute samples to 270 μL with PBS.
Treat samples with 30 μL of 10× CuAAC solution II.
Incubate samples for 6 h at 20°C–25°C under shaking (400 rpm).
Precipitate samples with 3 mL of cold methanol (10-fold excess) for 16–20 h at −80°C.
Centrifuge samples for 20 min at 3700 × g and 4°C.
Discard supernatant.
Add 3 mL of cold methanol (10-fold excess).
Centrifuge samples for 20 min at 3700 × g and 4°C.
Discard supernatant.
Repeat wash with 3 mL of cold methanol.
Discard supernatant.
Place the tubes upside down on tissue paper and air-dry the pellets to completely remove the methanol.
Resuspend pellets with 250 μL of 0.1% (w/v) RapiGest in PBS.
Sonicate samples in a water bath for 25 min.
Centrifuge samples for 5 min at 3700 × g.
Collect supernatant.
Resuspend pellets with 250 μL of 6 M urea in PBS.
Sonicate samples in a water bath for 25 min.
Centrifuge samples for 5 min at 3700 × g.
Collect supernatant.
Resuspend pellets with 250 μL of PBS.
Sonicate samples in a water bath for 25 min.
Centrifuge samples for 5 min at 3700 × g.
Collect supernatant.
Combine RapiGest, urea and PBS supernatants.
Transfer 350 μL of Lys-dimethylated Sera-Mag SpeedBeads Neutravidin-Coated Magnetic Beads slurry to low-bind tubes.
Place the beads on a magnetic rack and wait until the beads have migrated to the tube wall.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 200 μL of PBS.
Vortex briefly to resuspend the beads.
Spin down to ensure that all the solution is at the bottom of the tube.
Place the tubes on a magnetic rack and discard the supernatant.
Repeat wash with 200 μL of PBS.
Add the combined RapiGest, urea and PBS supernatants to the beads.
Vortex briefly to ensure the beads are in solution.
Incubate for 2 h at 20°C–25°C under rotation.
Wash beads three times with 350 μL of 1% (w/v) RapiGest in PBS.
Wash beads six times with 350 μL of 6 M urea in PBS.
Wash beads six times with 350 μL of AmBic.
Wash beads four times with 100 μL of 40% (v/v) LC/MS-grade acetonitrile in LC/MS-grade water.
Resuspend beads in 100 μL of AmBic containing 10 mM DTT to reduce disulfide bonds.
Incubate beads for 15 min at 50°C under shaking at 400 rpm.
Wash beads twice with 350 μL of AmBic.
Add 100 μL of 20 mM iodoacetamide in AmBic to alkylate the reduced disulfide bonds.
Incubate beads in the dark for 30 min at 20°C–25°C.
Add 100 μL of AmBic containing 10 mM DTT to neutralize iodoacetamide.
Discard supernatant.
Wash beads three times with 350 μL of AmBic.
Resuspend beads with 100 μL of AmBic.
Add 300 ng of Lys-C (i.e., 3 μL of the 0.1 μg/μL stock) to the beads.
Incubate samples for 16–20 h at 37°C under shaking at 400 rpm.
Transfer supernatant to a new tube.
Add 200 ng of trypsin (i.e., 2 μL of the 0.1 μg/μL stock) to the samples.
Incubate samples for 8 h at 37°C under shaking at 400 rpm.
Vacuum-dry samples by SpeedVac.
Add 150 μL of 1% (v/v) formic acid in LC/MS-grade water to the beads.
Cleave the acid-cleavable biotin probe and release glycopeptides bound to beads.
Incubate samples for 30 min at 20°C–25°C on a rotator.
Collect supernatant.
Repeat acid treatment.
Wash beads with 150 μL of LC/MS-grade acetonitrile.
Combine wash and collected supernatants.
Vacuum-dry samples by SpeedVac.
Reconstitute samples in 100 μL of AmBic.
Add 200 ng of trypsin (i.e., 2 μL of the 0.1 μg/μL stock) to the samples.
Incubate samples for 8 h at 37°C under shaking at 400 rpm.
Vacuum-dry samples by SpeedVac.
Condition UltraMicroSpin™ column: Add 100 μL of conditioning solvent to the column.
Use a 1 mL syringe attached to an applicator to push the liquid through the column.
Discard flow-through.
Repeat conditioning step.
Reconstitute sample in 100 μL of loading buffer.
Load sample on the column.
Use a 1 mL syringe attached to an applicator to push the liquid through the column.
Discard flow-through.
Wash column: Add 50 μL of wash buffer to the column to wash any traces of salts.
Use a 1 mL syringe attached to an applicator to push the liquid through the column.
Discard flow-through.
Elute sample: Place the UltraMicroSpin™ column in a clean 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 50 μL of elution buffer to the column.
Use a 1 mL syringe attached to an applicator to push the liquid through the column.
Collect flow-through.
Vacuum-dry the eluted sample to remove traces of organic solvent.
Store the vacuum-dried sample at -80°C.
Treat lysates with PNGase F prior to the click reaction for specific O-GalNAc glycan characterization.
Use Protein LoBind® Tubes throughout the procedure to minimize protein-surface binding and sample loss.
Store whole cell lysates at -20°C before performing the click reaction.
Store clicked lysates at -20°C after the click reaction before protein precipitation.
Combine supernatants after protein precipitation and resuspend them; store combined supernatants at -20°C prior to enrichment.
Store dried pellets before sample desalting at -80°C.
Store dried pellets after sample desalting at -80°C.
Prepare Buffer A: Mix 0.1% formic acid in LC/MS-grade water.
Prepare Buffer B: Mix 0.1% formic acid in LC/MS-grade acetonitrile.
Reconstitute dried samples with 16 μL of Buffer A.
Sonicate samples in a water bath for 15 min.
Vortex the samples briefly.
Centrifuge samples for 5 min at 18,000 × g.
Transfer the supernatant to a glass screw neck vial.
Load samples via autosampler and inject using a flow rate of 0.3 μL/min onto an EASY-Spray column containing 2 μm C18 beads.
Hold columns at 40°C using a column heater in the EASY-Spray ionization source.
Chromatographically separate the sample using a 75 min gradient and a 105 min instrument method.
Set up the instrument to acquire data in a dependent fashion using only higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD).
Set MS1 precursor mass resolution to 60,000 at full width at half maximum (FWHM) 400 m/z.
Set mass range for full mass spectra to 350–1,500 m/z and sample charge states 2–6.
Set the precursor automated gain control (AGC) settings to 3e5 ions.
Set the isolation window for HCD to 1.6 Da and collision energy to 30.
Enable dynamic exclusion with a repeat count of 3, repeat duration of 10 s, and an exclusion duration of 10 s.
Generate MS2 spectra using an Orbitrap at top speed for 3 s.
Set the precursor AGC settings to 3e5 ions.
Isolate precursors with an isolation window of 1.6 Da for HCD.
Apply a collision energy setting of 30 for HCD.

Select “Targeted Mass Trigger” for ETD if: (a) the precursor mass is between 300 and 1000 m/z, and (b) in the HCD spectrum, at least two glyco-fingerprint ions are present at +/- 20 ppm with greater than 5% relative intensity.
Calibrate charge-dependent ETD times.
Set reagent target to 2e5.
Set precursor AGC target to 1e4.
Read out fragment ions in the ion trap using centroid mode.
Configure gradient profile as follows: (minute:%B): 0:2, 5:2, 80:35, 85:95, 90:95, 92:2, 105:2.
Perform a database search using MaxQuant.
Load raw mass spectrometry files.
Select Set experiment to name each sample.
In the Group-specific parameters section, select Standard and set Multiplicity to 1.
Include methionine oxidation and N-terminal acetylation as variable modifications.
Include cysteine carbamidomethylation as a fixed modification with a total common max of 5.
Modify default parameters in Instrument based on the instrument used.
Select Specific in Digestion mode.
Select Trypsin/P as the Enzyme.
Allow two missed cleavages.
Select None for Label free quantification.
Add the Homo sapiens FASTA file from UniProt in Sequences.
Click on Identifier rule button and select the UniProt identifier if not automatically filled.
Click on Test to test parse rules.
Tick to include contaminants.
Tick iBAQ in Label free quantification.
Select the number of processors based on the instrument used.
Press Start to initiate the search.
Upload the proteinGroups.txt file.
In Main, select iBAQ for each sample.
In Categorical, select Taxonomy IDs and Peptide IDs.
Filter rows based on Reverse categorical column by selecting Reverse in column, Remove matching rows in mode, Reduce matrix in filter mode.
Filter rows based on Potential contaminant categorical column by selecting Potential contaminant in column, Remove matching rows in mode, Reduce matrix in filter mode.
Select OK.
In the Annotate rows function, select Categorical annotation rows.
In Row name type Technical replicates.
For each sample, make sure the replicates have the same name for the iBAQ columns (e.g., Exp1, Exp2, ...).
Select OK.
In the Annotate columns function, select Add annotation.
In Source select the .txt file containing the annotations for Homo sapiens derived from Uniprot and downloaded from http://annotations.perseus-framework.org.
In UniProt column select Protein IDs.
In Annotations to be added select Corum, Keywords, Taxonomy and UniProt names.
Select OK.
In the Normalization function, select Subtract.
In Matrix access select Columns.
In Subtract what select Median.
Select OK.
Use the Transform function on the matrix produced to transform the data to a logarithmic base.
In Transformation select log2(x).
In Columns select the iBAQ columns.
Select OK.
Use the Replace missing values from normal distribution function to make sure that all the datapoints have a numerical value.
Leave default parameters for Width, Down shift and Mode untouched.
In Columns select the iBAQ columns.
Select OK.
Use the Two sample test function to statistically analyze the data.
In Grouping select Technical replicates.
In First group (right) and Second group (left) select the two samples to be analyzed.
In Test select Welch’s T-test.
In Use for truncation select p-value.
Select OK.
Use the Scatter plot function to visualize the data produced.
Search raw files with 10 ppm mass tolerance for precursor mass ions.
Use 20 ppm and 0.2 Da fragment mass tolerances for HCD and ETD fragmentation, respectively.
Allow up to two missed cleavages per peptide and semi-specific C-terminal tryptic digestion (R,K cleavage sites).
Set a 1% false discovery rate using standard reverse-decoy techniques.
Specify methionine oxidation and asparagine deamidation as variable modifications with a total common max of 2, rare max of 1.
Set carbamidomethyl as a fixed modification.
Select “Create focused database” under the “Advanced” tab in Byonic interface to create a FASTA file containing only proteins found in the sample.
Edit the existing Byonic parameter file by selecting the focused database FASTA file.
Add modifications specified for glycans under the “Glycans” tab.
Search data again with updated parameters including glycan modifications.
Open the Excel file of search output and sort by “Glycans.”
Move rows with annotated glycans to a new sheet and sort by |Log Prob|.
Remove entries with a Log Prob value less than 3.
Sort the file by Score and remove anything with a score less than 100.
Sort the excel file by “Protein Rank”.
Open the Byonic Viewer.
Manually examine the HCD spectra of any remaining glycopeptides in the excel file.
Check if each HCD spectrum with a GalN6yne modified peptide contains an oxonium ion at 491 and another at 330.
Ensure that the peptide has at least 50% of the naked b/y ions annotated.
If the peptide meets these criteria, move on to the next step.
Otherwise, the peptide is not correctly annotated and should not be counted as a modified glycopeptide.
Extract the associated chromatograph in Qual Browser along with the associated ETD MS2 spectra.
Average the MS2 spectra generated.
De novo sequence the glycopeptide to identify which site is modified.
